The present application under Section 439 Cr.P.C. has been filed by the applicant Vineet Tiwari S/o Ashok Tiwari seeking bail in FIR/ Case Crime No. 156 of 2022 under Sections 366, 376, 328 and 506 IPC, Police Station Ibrahimpur, District Ambedkar Nagar.

sentences.text: As per the first information report the prosecutrix Neha Sharma, aged around 23 years, on 2nd July 2022 at around 6 p.m. had gone to the market to buy some clothes and did not come back till 14th July 2022.
The complainant/father of the prosecutrix has stated that one person with phone numbers 8858756334 and 7983996327 used to speak on the mobile number of his house being No. 6306897433.

The complainant had said to the said person that if he wanted to marry the prosecutrix, he would arrange the marriage, but the said person said that he would not marry her, but would sell her to someone else.
The prosecutrix came home and in her statements recorded under sections 161 and 164, CrPC she said that she had gone to the market on 2nd July 2022.
There she met with the accused-applicant, who is friend of her brother.
The accused-applicant offered her drink and after consuming the drink she became unconscious.
When she gained consciousness, she found herself at distant place and also found that she had been raped.
The accused-applicant handed over her to Saddam, who raped her for more than one month.
Considering the aforesaid facts and also the stand of the prosecutrix this court does not deem it appropriate to enlarge the accused-applicant on bail at this stage.
The bail-application is rejected.
Once the prosecutrix gets examined in the court as witness, the accused-applicant may revive the bail-plea, if he is so advised.
The District Superintendent of Police, Ambedkar Nagar, is directed to ensure arrest of the co-accused Saddam at the earliest.
Let a copy of this order be forwarded to the Superintendent of Police, Ambedkar Nagar for compliance."

This Court while rejecting the first bail application of the accused-applicant gave a liberty to the present accused-applicant that he may revive his bail-plea again after the prosecutrix gets examined in the trial court.
The prosecutrix has been examined in the trial court and her evidence has been placed on record which is annexed as Annexure No.10 to this second bail application.

Considering the submissions of learned counsel for the parties, the fact that the prosecutrix has been examined in the trial court and has not supported the prosecution case, this Court deem it appropriate to enlarge/release the accused-applicant on bail.
In view of the above, the present second bail application is allowed.

Let the applicant-Vineet Tiwari, who is involved in aforementioned case crime be released on bail on his furnishing a personal bond and two sureties each in the like amount to the satisfaction of the court concerned subject to following conditions.
(i) The applicant shall file an undertaking to the effect that he shall not seek any adjournment on the date fixed for evidence when the witnesses are present in Court.

In case of default of this condition,
it shall be open for the Trial Court to treat it as abuse of liberty of bail and pass orders in accordance with law.
(ii) The applicant shall remain present before the Trial Court on each date fixed, either personally or through his counsel.
In case of his absence, without sufficient cause, the Trial Court may proceed against him under Section 229-A IPC.

(iii) In case, the applicant misuses the liberty of bail during trial and in order to secure his presence proclamation under Section 82 Cr.P.C., may be issued and if applicant fails to appear before the Court on the date fixed in such proclamation, then, the Trial Court shall initiate proceedings against him, in accordance with law, under Section 174-A IPC.

(iv) The applicant shall remain present, in person, before the Trial Court on dates fixed for (1)
opening of the case, (2) framing of charge and (3) recording of statement under Section 313 Cr.P.C.
If in the opinion of the Trial Court absence of the applicant is deliberate or without sufficient cause,
then it shall be open for the Trial Court to treat such default as abuse of liberty of bail and proceed against him in accordance with law.
In case of breach of any of the above conditions, it shall be a ground for cancellation of bail.
